name: TV Guide shows
description: A scrolling listings channel made from your own schedule, in the style of the 1990s Prevue Channel or the 2000s TV Guide Channel, with information, round-the-clock ads or another channel's picture up top and music or a channel's sound. Needs Chrome or Edge on this computer.
author: SchedularrTV
lowPowerNotice: the scrolling listings are drawn by a hidden browser without a graphics chip and encoded live. Keep the top panel on Information (commercials or a channel there are extra encodes) and capture at 10 to 15 frames per second.

settings.label: Browser
settings.description: Chrome, Edge or Chromium, run hidden to draw the guide. Leave empty to find one automatically.
settings.lowPowerNote: On Raspberry Pi OS, install chromium (sudo apt install chromium); Chrome and Edge have no ARM Linux builds.

settings.label: ffmpeg
settings.description: Leave empty to use the ffmpeg set under App settings.

settings.label: Stream address
settings.description: How ErsatzTV reaches this scheduler. Leave empty unless ErsatzTV runs on another machine or in a container.

settings.label: Capture frames per second
settings.description: How often the guide is captured (5 to 30). Higher scrolls more smoothly but uses more CPU; the stream's own frame rate is set under App settings → Hardware and video encoding.
settings.lowPowerNote: 10 to 15 here (12 is the default): the listings never stop moving, so every captured frame is new work.

settings.label: Keep a guide running after it goes off air (seconds)
settings.description: So back-to-back guide segments don't restart the browser each time.

settings.label: Draw animations at the capture rate
settings.description: The hidden browser scrolls the listings (and moves anything else) only as often as they're captured, instead of redrawing 60 times a second for frames that are never used. They scroll at the same speed. Turn off only if something stops or stutters.

settings.label: Decode the video window on the graphics chip
settings.description: Let the graphics chip decode the channel or commercials in the video window instead of the processor (ffmpeg's -hwaccel). auto picks one if there is one; cuda is NVIDIA, qsv Intel, d3d11va any card on Windows, vaapi Intel or AMD on Linux, videotoolbox a Mac. Video it can't decode is decoded in software instead. To encode on the graphics chip too, choose its encoder under App settings, Hardware and video encoding, Live page channels.
settings.lowPowerNote: The Pi's chip decodes HEVC but not H.264 this way, so this saves little for ErsatzTV's H.264 channels.
